paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.
model_annotation: The line chart displays the average cosine similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models as a function of the size of the subset, denoted |S|, which is plotted on the x-axis with a linear scale ranging from 2 to 10 in integer increments. The y-axis represents cosine similarity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.1 to 0.5. The blue dashed line with square markers, labeled “Weight averaging,” starts at a cosine similarity of approximately 0.49 at |S| = 2 and gradually decreases to approximately 0.31 at |S| = 10, showing a consistent downward trend with minor fluctuations. The green dashed line with circular markers, labeled “QAdapter,” begins at approximately 0.37 at |S| = 2 and steadily declines to approximately 0.20 at |S| = 10, maintaining a relatively smooth and consistent downward trajectory without significant fluctuations.
